title.es: Guion de una charla de dos minutos

es: Escribir el guion de una charla de dos minutos sobre un tema personal, con una apertura que cree cercanía, al menos tres señalizadores, una tendencia descrita con cifras y aproximaciones, y un cierre que refuerce el mensaje.

vocabulary.es: buena relación, conexión con el público

teaching.en: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words, so the script must be punchy: short sentences, one idea each and no padding.
teaching.es: Una charla de dos minutos tiene unas doscientas palabras, así que el guion debe ser directo: frases cortas, una idea por frase y nada de relleno.
teaching.explanationEs: Script: el texto que escribes para decir en voz alta; punchy = corto, claro y con fuerza.
segments: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words, so the script
must be punchy: short sentences, one idea each and no padding.
teaching.audioText: A two-minute talk has about two hundred words, so the script must be punchy: short sentences, one idea each and no padding.

teaching.en: She begins by greeting the audience and naming her topic, because a clear opening builds rapport before the first figure appears.
teaching.es: Empieza saludando al público y nombrando su tema, porque una apertura clara crea conexión antes de que aparezca la primera cifra.
teaching.explanationEs: Apertura: saludo + tema; build rapport = crear buena relación con quien escucha.
segments: She begins by greeting the audience and naming her topic, because
a clear opening builds rapport before the first figure appears.
teaching.audioText: She begins by greeting the audience and naming her topic, because a clear opening builds rapport before the first figure appears.

teaching.en: She will introduce each new point with a signpost such as firstly or now let's move on, and she will drive home her main message at the end.
teaching.es: Presentará cada punto nuevo con una señal como «firstly» o «now let's move on» y dejará muy claro su mensaje principal al final.
teaching.explanationEs: Introduce each point: los señalizadores de la clase 86; drive home = grabar la idea central en la mente del público.
segments: She will introduce each new point with a signpost such as firstly or now
let's move on, and she will drive home her main message at the end.
teaching.audioText: She will introduce each new point with a signpost such as firstly or now let's move on, and she will drive home her main message at the end.

teaching.en: Her script describes a trend: membership rose from twelve to thirty in a year, which she calls a steady climb rather than a sudden jump.
teaching.es: Su guion describe una tendencia: el número de socios subió de doce a treinta en un año, lo que ella llama un ascenso constante y no un salto repentino.
teaching.explanationEs: La tendencia lleva un verbo de cambio, from… to… y un periodo; rather than contrasta dos descripciones.
segments: Her script describes a trend: membership rose from twelve to thirty in a
year, which she calls a steady climb rather than a sudden jump.
teaching.audioText: Her script describes a trend: membership rose from twelve to thirty in a year, which she calls a steady climb rather than a sudden jump.

teaching.en: A good speaker keeps a steady pace, takes a short pause after each key point and never lets the talk run over the time limit.
teaching.es: Un buen orador mantiene un ritmo constante, hace una breve pausa tras cada punto clave y nunca deja que la charla se pase del tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Pace: velocidad al hablar; pause: parada breve que deja pensar; run over = exceder el tiempo previsto.
segments: A good speaker keeps a steady pace, takes a short pause after each
key point and never lets the talk run over the time limit.
teaching.audioText: A good speaker keeps a steady pace, takes a short pause after each key point and never lets the talk run over the time limit.

teaching.en: I always rehearse aloud at least twice, because reading a script silently hides the sentences that sound awkward when spoken.
teaching.es: Siempre ensayo en voz alta al menos dos veces, porque leer un guion en silencio oculta las frases que suenan raras al decirlas.
teaching.explanationEs: Rehearse aloud: ensayar diciendo el texto para medir el tiempo y detectar frases difíciles de pronunciar.
segments: I always rehearse aloud at least twice, because reading a
script silently hides the sentences that sound awkward when spoken.

prompt.es: Elige la apertura que cumple las tres condiciones de la tarea.

choices.text: Good morning, everyone. My topic is our school book club, and I hope you will enjoy listening to me for two minutes.
Good morning, everyone. I will outline three points, starting with the background, then the results, and finally I will sum up.
Good morning, everyone. My topic is our school book club, and I will outline three points, starting with how it grew.

feedback.es: Solo la primera saluda, nombra el tema y anuncia el esquema con «I will outline three points»; las otras olvidan una de las tres condiciones: el esquema o el tema.

hint.es: Comprueba que haya saludo, tema y anuncio del esquema.

origin.text: Task: open a two-minute talk by greeting the audience, naming the topic and announcing how the talk is organised.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un buen orador siempre ensaya en voz alta al menos dos veces.»

feedback.es: Rehearse aloud es ensayar diciendo el texto en voz alta, lo que permite medir el tiempo y detectar frases difíciles.

origin.text: Reading a script silently hides awkward phrases, so a good speaker always rehearses ___ at least twice before the talk.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Haz una pausa breve tras cada punto para mantener el ritmo.»

answer.text: Take a short pause after each point to keep the pace

feedback.es: Take a pause + after each point indica cuándo parar, y to keep the pace explica para qué sirve la pausa.

hint.es: Empieza con Take a short pause.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del guion con la función que cumple.

pairs: Good morning, everyone. My topic is swimming.
Our club rose from twelve to thirty members in two years.
Now let's move on to the second part.
So remember: start small, but keep going.

pairs.es: mensaje final que se quiere grabar

feedback.es: Un guion combina saludo y tema, una tendencia con cifras, señalizadores de transición y un mensaje final memorable.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe estos datos con más precisión.

choices.text: Membership more than doubled by 2024, then hardly changed in 2025.
Membership rose steadily every year, from twelve to thirty-one.
Membership more than doubled by 2024, then fell slightly in 2025.

feedback.es: De 12 a 30 es más del doble, y de 30 a 31 apenas hay cambio (no una bajada); decir que subió de forma constante cada año deforma los datos.

origin.text: Club members: twelve in 2022, thirty in 2024 and thirty-one in 2025, according to the club's own report.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si se pasa del tiempo, recortamos el ejemplo menos importante.»

feedback.es: Run over significa exceder el tiempo previsto; en un guion breve es la señal para recortar.

origin.text: Our talk must stay within two minutes. If it starts to ___ over the time limit, we cut the least important example.

prompt.es: Elige el guion con mejor estructura de apertura, desarrollo y cierre.

choices.text: Good afternoon, everyone. My topic is swimming. Firstly, our club grew from twelve to thirty members. To sum up, swimming is popular. Now let's move on to the pool. Thank you.
Good afternoon, everyone. My topic is swimming. Firstly, our club grew from twelve to thirty members. Now let's move on to the pool: it is too small. To sum up, swimming is popular. Thank you.
Firstly, our club grew from twelve to thirty members. Good afternoon, everyone. My topic is swimming. Now let's move on to the pool: it is too small. Thank you. To sum up, swimming is popular.

feedback.es: Solo un guion ordena saludo, tema, señalizador, desarrollo y cierre; en los otros el resumen llega antes del último punto o el saludo llega después de los datos.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le recomienda la profesora para el final de la charla.

choices.text: Add a new example so the message sounds more convincing.
Read the ending faster so the talk fits into two minutes.
Cut an example so the closing can be delivered more slowly.

feedback.es: La profesora aprueba las cifras y la estructura, pero el final va con prisa: recomienda cortar un ejemplo y frenar el ritmo al cerrar.

origin.audio: After her two-minute talk, the student felt it had gone well, but her teacher disagreed. She said the figures were clear and the structure was easy to follow, yet the talk ran to nearly three minutes and the ending felt rushed. Her advice was to cut one example, slow the pace and pause after the main message so that it would stay in the audience's mind.

prompt.es: Completa: «Eligió frases cortas y directas para mantener el interés.»

feedback.es: Punchy describe frases cortas y con fuerza, que sostienen la atención mejor que las explicaciones largas.

origin.text: To keep the audience interested, she chose short, ___ sentences and avoided long explanations that might make people lose interest.

prompt.es: Escribe el guion de tu charla con tres señalizadores y una tendencia.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club has grown. As you can see in my chart, membership rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of the members are first-year students, and just under a third are boys. Finally, I would like to turn to our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew gradually and is ready for a new challenge. The message I want you to take home is simple: a few friends and a corridor were enough. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.
accepted: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club has grown. As you can see in my chart, membership rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of the members are first-year students, and just under a third are boys. Finally, I would like to turn to our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew gradually and is ready for a new challenge. The message I want you to take home is simple: a few friends and a corridor were enough. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.

Hello, everyone, and welcome. Today I want to present my hobby, which is running, and I will outline the talk in three parts: why I started, how my training changed and my next goal. Firstly, I started running two years ago because I wanted to feel healthier. At the beginning, I could run for only ten minutes without stopping. Let's move on to the second part: my training. As you can see in my chart, my weekly distance rose gradually, from roughly five to around twenty kilometres in one year. I also take a short pause between exercises, and I keep a steady pace. Now I'd like to turn to my goal for next year. I hope to run a half marathon in the spring, and my friends will run with me. To sum up, running is cheap, simple and good for the head as well as for the body. Thank you very much for listening. Are there any questions?

feedback.es: Un buen guion abre con saludo y tema, usa tres señalizadores, describe una tendencia con cifras y cierra con To sum up y una invitación a preguntas.

origin.text: Elige un tema personal (un hobby, un club, tu ciudad) y escribe el guion de una charla de dos minutos, de 190 a 240 palabras. Incluye: saludo y tema; al menos tres señalizadores (firstly, now let's move on to, to sum up…); una tendencia con cifras (rose gradually from… to…) con aproximaciones (roughly, just under); y un cierre que refuerce el mensaje con una invitación a preguntas.

evidenceGroups: now i'd like to turn to

prompt.es: ¿Qué le sugiere la profesora con este comentario sobre el borrador?

choices.text: To reduce the data and focus on a single message.
To put every figure on a chart rather than read it out.
To read the figures more slowly during the talk.

feedback.es: Si el público se pierde contando cifras, la solución es conservar solo dos y centrarse en un único mensaje.

origin.text: Teacher's comment on a draft: “You have many figures, and your research is careful. The trouble is that the audience will be counting numbers instead of listening to you, so I would keep two figures and drive home one message.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué decisión toma el orador y por qué.

choices.text: Reading faster, because the story is the real message.
Cutting the story, because the trend carries the message.
Dropping the trend, because it takes too long to explain.

feedback.es: Prefiere recortar la anécdota del tren antes que hablar más rápido, porque la tendencia es lo que quiere que el público recuerde.

origin.audio: I timed my talk yesterday and it took three minutes ten, which is too long for a two-minute talk. I could have read faster, but then nobody would follow me, so I will cut my story about the train and keep the trend, because the trend is the real message.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ensayé en voz alta y recorté dos frases para ganar ritmo.»

answer.text: I rehearsed aloud and cut two sentences to improve the pace

feedback.es: I rehearsed aloud cuenta lo que hizo y and cut two sentences to improve the pace da el motivo de los recortes.
